solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Phone left in recess

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for left sits inside the word for a recess

parts.note: a bower is a shady recess or arbour

explanation.surface: Someone has left their phone in an alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside BOWER. BLOWER is old British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is informal British slang for a telephone, from speaking tubes once blown into.

clue.text: European city, for example, featured in story

indicators.note: featured in says the abbreviation appears within the word for a story

parts.note: a lie is a story in the sense of a fib

explanation.surface: A tale features a particular European city as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a city shown as an example in a story; the city is the definition, and Liège is in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a large city in eastern Belgium, so it is a European city.

clue.text: Feel elated having small part broadcast

parts.note: a walk-on is a small non-speaking part in a play
to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An actor is thrilled that their small role is being shown on television.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on air is an idiom meaning to be overjoyed, as elated people feel weightless.

clue.text: Where plane lands makes fugitive lose heart

indicators.note: lose heart tells us to drop the central letter of the word for a fugitive

parts.note: a runaway is someone who has fled, a fugitive

explanation.surface: An escaped convict gives up hope at an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose heart' removes the middle A of RUNAWAY; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip of an airfield on which aircraft touch down.

clue.text: Extremely fashionable black suit

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
spades is one of the two black suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A very stylish black outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but is a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In spades is an idiom meaning in large amounts or to a great degree.

clue.text: Originally without appeal, where tour ends?

definitions.meaning: the phrase first described a court whose judgement could not be appealed further
a whimsical reading: the final holiday destination visited on a trip

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase first meant a final court beyond which no appeal lay, and literally could mean the last holiday spot.

clue.text: Serving up endless wine is ominous

indicators.note: in a down clue serving up means the pieces are presented reading upwards
endless means the final letter of the wine is dropped

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Constantly pouring wine is a bad sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts RETSINA to RETSIN; add IS to make RETSINIS, and 'Serving up' turns the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something threatening or suggesting harm, just as ominous does.

clue.text: Dressing made from first-rate oil abroad

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the figure one read as the letter I

indicators.note: abroad suggests the letters are scattered or astray, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A salad dressing made from top-quality foreign oil.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 gives AI; 'abroad' rearranges OIL into OLI; 'made from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise used as a sauce or dressing.

clue.text: Private individual

definitions.meaning: private here means restricted to a select few, as in a members-only club
individual here means belonging to one alone, not shared

explanation.definitionFit: Exclusive means restricted to particular people and also sole or unshared, matching both senses.

clue.text: With bandleader in capital

parts.note: Duke Ellington was the famous American jazz bandleader

explanation.surface: Joining the band's leader in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington is the capital city of New Zealand.

clue.text: Formerly working with church

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone used to be employed by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, which is what formerly says.

clue.text: Article in French daily exposing drink

indicators.note: in places the indefinite article inside the name of the newspaper

parts.note: Le Monde is a French daily newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A French newspaper story exposes something about a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside LE MONDE, after LEMON; 'exposing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink flavoured with lemon.

clue.text: Mistake made by fielder at Oxford?

parts.note: slip is a fielding position in cricket beside the wicketkeeper
up means at university, as a student is up at Oxford

explanation.surface: An error committed by a cricket fielder from Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIP is a cricket fielding position; British students are 'up' at university such as Oxford. 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is an informal word for an error or blunder.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory, a bygone king

parts.note: off means not up to standard, as in an off day

explanation.surface: A poor performance by an ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFA was an eighth-century king of Mercia, an Anglo-Saxon English kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled Mercia in the eighth century, so he is a king long gone.

clue.text: Good hand from capacity crowd

definitions.meaning: in poker, three of a kind plus a pair is a strong hand
a theatre with every seat sold has this

explanation.definitionFit: A full house is a strong poker hand and also a venue filled to capacity.

clue.text: Verse by Forster used in a song and a prayer

indicators.note: used in places the abbreviations within the article and song

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
E. M. Forster the novelist, whose initials are EM

explanation.surface: A verse by the novelist Forster appears in a song and a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Forster stands for his initials only; 'and a' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ave Maria, or Hail Mary, is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin.

clue.text: Vegetable all right to be eaten by ambassador on the wagon?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed below the wagon

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British term for a big truck

indicators.note: to be eaten by puts the approval word inside the ambassador's title

parts.note: HE is His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A vegetable approved for eating by a teetotal diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wagon' looks like teetotal, but the wagon is an articulated lorry (British 'artic'). In a down clue 'on' puts the eaten-into piece below it.
explanation.definitionFit: An artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Weaker party grounded, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The weaker side has been grounded, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges GROUNDED.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the competitor expected to lose, the weaker side.

clue.text: Musical instrument popular in Bordeaux

indicators.note: in places the word for popular within the name of the wine

parts.note: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A woodwind instrument that is popular in the Bordeaux region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordeaux' looks like the place, but is its wine, CLARET.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Before end of encounter, draw level

indicators.note: before means the word for draw comes ahead of the final letter

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Just before a match finishes, the score is level.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE goes 'Before' R, the last letter of 'encounter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or row in a stepped arrangement, such as seating.

clue.text: Planes (American) abandoned cargo

parts.note: jets are planes

explanation.surface: American aircraft dumped their cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is goods thrown overboard from a ship to lighten it, cargo deliberately discarded.

clue.text: Terrible rage after child makes accusation

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the abbreviation for child
terrible indicates the letters are in a dreadful mess

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of a dreadful tantrum after dealing with a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible rage' reads as a tantrum, but 'Terrible' is the anagram signal and only RAGE is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a formal accusation of an offence.

clue.text: Splendid beer served up

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the beer is read upwards

parts.note: lager is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A fine beer is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns LAGER upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means fit for a monarch, hence magnificent or splendid.

clue.text: Work out problem

definitions.meaning: to work out is to train the body
a problem set for practice, as in a school task

explanation.definitionFit: Exercise means physical training and also a set task or problem for practice.

clue.text: Give out letters in magic formula

definitions.meaning: to name the letters of a word in order

explanation.definitionFit: To spell is to say a word's letters in order, and a spell is an incantation or charm.

clue.text: Flaw detected round edge of crown cork

indicators.note: round says the word for flaw goes around the picked letter

parts.note: a bug is a flaw, as in software

indicators.note: edge of picks the end letter of crown

explanation.surface: A defect spotted around the rim of a crown cork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge of' gives N, the end of 'crown'; 'round' puts BUG around it. 'detected' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a stopper for a barrel or bottle, much like a cork.

clue.text: Pancakes — declines cold ones

parts.note: drops means declines, as prices fall
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone refuses the cold pancakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declines' looks like refuses, but means falls. Drop scones are small thick British pancakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop scones are small thick pancakes made by dropping batter onto a griddle.

clue.text: One may get led astray in just this sort of district!

definitions.text: One may get led astray in just this sort of district!

parts.words: One may get led astray in just this sort of district!
parts.note: a sly description of a city area known for prostitution, where a visitor may be tempted

explanation.definitionFit: A red-light district is an area of a town where brothels and sex shops cluster.

clue.text: Dish produced by Greek character on foreign isle

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish made by a Greek on an island abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges ISLE into ESLI; 'produced by' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast dish of oats, nuts and dried fruit.
